samples.summary: Cell-style attribute removal uses a *range* over the whole cell subtree, so `backgroundColor` is also stripped from every inline (text highlight) and nested-table node inside the cell
samples.evidence: `applyCellStyle` now does `tree.removeStyleByPath(cellPath, endPath, removeAttrs)` with `endPath = [...cellPath]` and last index +1 — a position range that spans the cell node AND all of its descendants (blocks, inlines, nested tables). Yorkie's tree style/removeStyle applies to every non-text node in the range (the same reason `setBlockType`'s `removeStyleByPath(blockPath, blockPath+1, ['listKind','listLevel'])` at line 1439 reaches inline nodes too — harmlessly, because those keys don't exist there). Here the attribute name collides: inline nodes store text highlight under the very same key `backgroundColor` (`serializeInlineStyle` line 122, `parseInlineStyle` line 177), and nested table cells store `backgroundColor`/`border*`/`padding`. So the new "No fill" reset (docs-table-context-menu.tsx:233 → `{ backgroundColor: undefined }`) silently deletes the highlight colour of every run in the cell and the fills/borders of any nested table — irreversible data loss in the CRDT. The in-memory cache is only patched for the cell (`cell.style = merged`), so the loss is invisible until reload/remote sync, and the added test (yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:2031) uses a cell whose inlines have no `backgroundColor`, so it cannot catch this. A per-node removal (or an explicit `removeStyleByPath` restricted to the cell element only, e.g. by re-setting the descendants' attrs) is needed.

samples.summary: `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS` lookup is not actually closed — prototype keys (`toString`, `constructor`, `__proto__`, `valueOf`) resolve to inherited values that get interpolated into `w:jc/@w:val`
samples.evidence: `const align = DOCX_ALIGNMENTS[style.alignment as string] ?? 'left'` indexes a plain object literal, so the prototype chain is consulted. `style.alignment === 'toString'` yields `Object.prototype.toString` (a function), which is `!== 'left'` and is stringified into `<w:jc w:val="function toString() { [native code] }"/>`; `'__proto__'` yields `[object Object]`. The doc comment above claims `w:jc w:val` "can only ever carry an ST_Jc token", which is false — the result is a schema-invalid `ST_Jc` value that Word can refuse to open, i.e. the exact failure the change set out to prevent. Use `Object.hasOwn(DOCX_ALIGNMENTS, ...)`, a `Map`/`Set`, or `Object.create(null)`. The same pattern exists in the slides sink the comment cites as the model (`packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:79`, `ALGN[block.style.alignment] ?? 'l'`), so it is not clamped there either.

samples.summary: The new `style.alignment` value check is bypassed by the slides content PUT path, contradicting the guard's own rationale
samples.evidence: `assertValidBlockStyle` is only reached through `assertValidDocsBody` → `assertValidBlock`. The slides body validator (`assertValidSlidesBody` → `assertValidSlide` → `assertValidElement`, lines 376–435) checks only `id`/`type`/`frame` and never walks a text element's docs `blocks`, so an arbitrary `style.alignment` string still lands in the CRDT for slides documents and reaches both the PPTX (`ALGN[...]`) and any docs-block export sink. read assertValidSlidesBody, assertValidSlide, assertValidElement in docs-content.controller.ts

samples.summary: `isEmptyStoredColor` dereferences `c.value` without a type guard, so a malformed `{ kind: 'srgb' }` (no `value`) now throws where the previous code silently resolved to `undefined`
samples.evidence: `return c.kind === 'srgb' && c.value.trim() === ''` — `c.value` is typed `string` but the value comes from persisted/imported CRDT JSON. Before this change, such an object flowed into `defaultColorResolver`, which returned `c.value` (`undefined`) harmlessly; now `.trim()` on `undefined` raises a TypeError inside the render/caret path (`resolveColorAtPosition`, painters). Real, reachable, irreversible CRDT attribute loss: in-lane (data loss / broken invariant) and blocking.

'left'` indexes a plain object literal, so the prototype chain is consulted. `style.alignment === 'toString'` yields `Object.prototype.toString` (a function), which is `!== 'left'` and is stringified into `<w:jc w:val="function toString() { [native code] }"/>`; `'__proto__'` yields `[object Object]`. verdict.reason: Verified in the repo. docx-style-map.ts:115-120 defines DOCX_ALIGNMENTS as a plain object literal, and line 141 indexes it with `style.alignment as string`, so prototype keys ('toString', 'constructor', 'valueOf', '__proto__') resolve to inherited values instead of undefined; `??` does not catch them, line 142's `align !== 'left'` passes, and line 143 interpolates them into `<w:jc w:val="...">`, yielding schema-invalid ST_Jc values like `function toString() { [native code] }` or `[object Object]` — directly contradicting the "closed map / can only ever carry an ST_Jc token" comment at lines 111-113 and 138-140. The same hole exists in the cited slides model at slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:61-66,79. It is not already-guarded: the backend Set-based check (docs-content.controller.ts:254,266-279) covers only the content-PUT entry point, while the CRDT read path casts alignment blindly (yorkie/docs-tree.ts:157-158) and normalizeBlockStyle (docs/src/model/types.ts:272-274) merely spreads defaults without clamping, so an arbitrary persisted alignment reaches the sink. A guard whose fallback fails to fire and emits corrupt output that Word can refuse to open is a real correctness defect (wrong condition / broken invariant), not a security-only concern.

mergedFrom.summary: `resolveStoredColor` normalizes only the bare `''` before the resolver, so the `{ kind: 'srgb', value: '' }` form the PPTX exporter explicitly guards against still bypasses the theme branch

finding.summary: `resolveStoredColor` only collapses the bare `''` before the resolver, so the `{ kind: 'srgb', value: '' }` form the docstring calls reachable lands on the docs default instead of the theme color
finding.evidence: `return resolve(c === '' ? undefined : c) || undefined;` — the pre-resolver normalization matches only the string `''`. For `{ kind: 'srgb', value: '' }` (a shape the function's own doc comment and the new PPTX test both call reachable) slides' `makeColorResolver` → `resolveColor` (slides/src/model/theme.ts:100-116) returns `''`, which the trailing `|| undefined` turns into `undefined`, so `renderRun`/`renderListMarker` fall back to `theme.defaultColor` (docs near-black) rather than the deck theme's text color. That is exactly the dark-deck failure the comment says the 'before' half exists to prevent, just for the object arm.

verdict.reason: The finding quotes `return resolve(c === '' ? undefined : c) || undefined;` as the body of `resolveStoredColor`, but that code does not exist in this repository. packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:51 reads `return resolve(isEmptyStoredColor(c) ? undefined : c) || undefined;`, and `isEmptyStoredColor` (color.ts:59-63) returns true for BOTH the bare string arm (`c.trim() === ''`) and the object arm (`c.kind === 'srgb' && c.value.trim() === ''`). A repo-wide grep for the quoted expression `c === '' ? undefined : c` yields no matches. Therefore `{ kind: 'srgb', value: '' }` IS collapsed to `undefined` before the resolver runs, the theme-aware resolver takes its "no color set" branch, and the docs-default/dark-deck failure mode described never occurs for that input. This is confirmed by an existing test (packages/docs/test/model/color.test.ts:210-218) asserting that `resolveStoredColor(themeAware, { kind: 'srgb', value: '' })` returns the theme color '#ffffff' and that the resolver was called with `undefined` (`seen` === `[undefined]`). Because the empty value is normalized pre-resolver, slides' `resolveColor` is never handed the empty srgb object and the trailing `|| undefined` fallback path the finding relies on is unreachable for this case. The described code is not present.

finding.summary: Table-cell "No fill" reset still cannot clear the stored fill — the #728 reset class the diff fixes for runs is left broken for cells
finding.evidence: The diff fixes run color/highlight resets by passing `undefined` (handled by `removedInlineStyleAttrs` + `tree.removeStyleByPath`, yorkie-doc-store.ts:144/1881). The cell path was not updated: `docs-table-context-menu.tsx:230` calls `editor.applyTableCellStyle({ backgroundColor: "" })`; `serializeCellStyle` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:238) does `if (s.backgroundColor) attrs.backgroundColor = ...`, so the empty string is dropped from the attribute map, and `applyCellStyle` (line 2426) only calls `tree.styleByPath(...)` with no `removeStyleByPath`. Because `styleByPath` merges, the previous `backgroundColor` attribute survives in the CRDT: locally the cache shows `''` (renders as no fill), but the fill reappears for peers and after reload. Same root cause as issue #728, one call site away from the guard the diff added.

verdict.reason: Every element of the claimed absence is present in this tree. (1) The reset call site does NOT pass an empty string: docs-table-context-menu.tsx:233 calls `editor.applyTableCellStyle({ backgroundColor: undefined })`, with a comment at :230-232 explicitly referencing issue #728 and the need to remove rather than merge over. (2) The cell-side analogue of `removedInlineStyleAttrs` exists: `removedCellStyleAttrs` at yorkie-doc-store.ts:255-261 returns keys where `key in style && style[key] === undefined` for backgroundColor, verticalAlign, padding and the four border keys. (3) `applyCellStyle` does not only call `styleByPath`: yorkie-doc-store.ts:2437 computes `removeAttrs = removedCellStyleAttrs(style)` and :2448-2452 calls `tree.removeStyleByPath(cellPath, endPath, removeAttrs)` right after `tree.styleByPath` (:2447), so the stale attribute really leaves the CRDT for peers and after reload. I also traced the intermediate hops to rule out the explicitly-undefined key being stripped before reaching the store: editor.ts:3648-3671 forwards `style` unchanged to `doc.applyCellStyle`, which forwards it unchanged to `store.applyCellStyle` (document.ts:856-863), so the `in`-operator test still sees the key. The local cache is consistent too (`merged` at :2429 yields backgroundColor: undefined), and tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:2040 exercises `{ backgroundColor: undefined }`. The finding describes a state of the code that does not exist here.
